summary: The runtime restart owner (openclawGatewayClient --deploy-restart and /v1/runtime/restart) now adopts a Gateway it did not launch, identified by the OpenClaw gateway-owner lease (start time checked) or by the Gateway server process on the same state directory; the stop is graceful for up to 15 s before SIGKILL, leftover workers are stopped by start-time identity, a Gateway of another state directory is never awaited nor killed, the restart verdict reaches the deploy log and runtime-sync allows 360 s.
reason: S24 01/11 21:06: companion-deploy d55ad8f6 and its rollback ended in gateway_restart_failed. The OpenClaw 2026.10.9 Gateway (PID 22573, ppid 1) had been started by openclaw-upgrade, which writes no Companion pidfile; the pidfile still named the stopped 9.6 Gateway, so the owner selected zero stop targets and reported 'still reachable' after about 11 s (replayed on the S24 and confirmed by POST /v1/runtime/restart: 500 in 11.05 s, Gateway untouched).
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the previous commit with companion-deploy.sh; a plugin-changing deploy then fails again with gateway_restart_failed while a Gateway started outside the Companion is running.

routes.change: same contract; adoption of the live Gateway of this state directory, graceful stop, failure message states the target count
routes.budget: stop grace 15 s + stop wait 10 s + start 180 s; runtime-sync client 360 s (was 240 s)

architecture.reason: Same canonical runtime owner and lease helper; adoption mirrors the identity already used by openclaw-upgrade. No new store, daemon, scheduler or retry.

limitations: openclaw-upgrade still logs the Gateway in ~/.openclaw/logs while the Companion logs in workspace/logs; unchanged here.
The health-manager restart clients keep their 230 s budget; the server-side restart is not aborted by a client timeout.
